schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo; 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. commit 733daffd5a0f9d37a62cc6dc4f9dbe121c314085
Author: Kenneth Jiang <kenneth.jiang@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Nov 15 20:44:47 2026 -0800

    Report unexpected errors to the JusPrin team, and stop explaining five that can't happen
    
    When something fails that no person can act on, JusPrin now shows one
    dialog, "Something went wrong on our side" (boards agent-ui-11 to 16),
    instead of a sentence about that particular failure. The person can see
    the whole report, press "Report to JusPrin team", or tick "From now on,
    report errors like this automatically". The report goes to JusPrin's
    server (/ent/jusprin/v2/error_reports), which passes it to Sentry.
    
    Why: under the error-handling rules in AGENTS.md, a failure with no
    outcome a person decided travels up unchanged to the top of its entry
    point, and is reported there, instead of each site writing its own
    sentence. Kenneth agreed to this on 2026-11-15: "Yes, go with this
    approach."
    
    The reporting path
    - Support/ErrorReport: report_unexpected_error() logs the error, then
      sends it at once when automatic reports are on, or queues it for the
      dialog after the current event. A failure that repeats while its
      dialog waits is queued once. A report holds the app and OS versions,
      what the app was doing, the error and, for page errors, the stack. The
      home folder becomes "~", a file-system error's paths become "<path>",
      and each field is cut to the server's limit. The send is anonymous: no
      token or cookie.
    - Shell/ErrorReportDialog: the dialog, drawn with the design tokens.
    - Top handlers: OrcaSlicer's main-loop exception hook (one line in
      GUI_App::OnExceptionInMainLoop; running out of memory still goes to
      OrcaSlicer's own handling), the AI pages' and Home's message handlers,
      and both pages' own top level (window "error" and
      "unhandledrejection", sent as a new report_error message and queued
      until the page has connected).
    - Preferences › Updates: a new "Error reports" box,
      "Report errors to the JusPrin team automatically", off by default.
    
    Five failures now take that path, with their sentences removed:
    - "JusPrin couldn't start signing in. Try again." (the AI page and Home)
    - "The file could not be read." (an attachment that is not base64, or a
      picked file that cannot be opened or read)
    - "The G-code couldn't be written to %s." (exporting from print history)
    - "The panel is still loading. Try again in a moment." (a printer or
      filament chat asked to reply before its page sent its instructions)
    - "The earlier values cannot be put back." (an undo the settings preview
      refuses without giving a reason)
    
    Six others stay as they are, on Kenneth's answer "Yes, keep them":
    signing in that did not finish, an unreadable import from another app,
    the AI models not loaded yet, the saved projects that could not be
    read, the open project that could not be saved, and projects that could
    not be loaded.
    
    New on-screen strings beyond the boards (the report's row names "App",
    "Was doing" and "Where", the singular forms of the two counted
    sentences, and the Preferences group, box and detail line) were shown to
    Kenneth, who answered "approved". All new strings are machine-translated
    into the 22 catalogs and marked "# AI Translated"; two are also marked
    "Needs human review" (the Lithuanian and Basque singular forms).

"Needs human review" (the Lithuanian and Basque singular forms).
    
    Tests
    - agent_bridge_tests (580 cases), jusprin_tests (178),
      jusprin_profile_tests (20) and shell_theme_tests (17) pass;
      brand_tokens_tests has its one known failure. AgentUI vitest (830,
      catalog completeness included) and the HomeUI tests pass; tsc is clean
      for both. These ran before the last change, which only touches
      Support/ErrorReport.cpp (not in any test target); the app was rebuilt
      and checked live after it.
    - Shown in a scratch copy of the app (its own data folder and HOME), with
      reports going through the local server to a stand-in Sentry:
      - sign-in that cannot start: the dialog opens; Cancel sends nothing.
      - an attachment that is not base64: the dialog opens; with the box
        ticked the button reads "Report this and future errors", the report
        arrives, and the setting is saved as on.
      - G-code export beside a file in a read-only folder: the dialog opens
        and the report arrives, with both paths shown as "<path>".
      - a printer chat whose page held back its instructions: the dialog
        opens and the report arrives. The person then sees their message
        with no reply under it and the reply box ready; each further
        message opens the dialog again.
      - an error thrown in the AI page's own script: the dialog opens and
        the report arrives.
      - the Preferences box: shown off, ticked, saved as on; the next error
        is sent with no dialog.
    - Unit tests only: a picked attachment that cannot be read from disk
      (needs a real drop or the file picker), and the undo refused without
      a reason. The undo case cannot happen in the real app:
      OrcaWorkspaceAdapter::preview_settings records a reason with every
      refusal, so only the fake workspace can produce it.
    
    OrcaSlicer-owned file
    - GUI_App.cpp gains two lines at the top of OnExceptionInMainLoop and
      nothing upstream is deleted or rewritten; the hook is reached through
      JusPrin/OrcaHooks.hpp, which GUI_App.cpp already includes. The fork
      now owns policy here: an exception that leaves an event handler is
      reported and the app keeps running. OrcaSlicer's own handler logs it
      and rethrows, which ends the app; it still handles running out of
      memory, which it ends the app for.
    - Rebase check: git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=v2.5.0
      (40ecc66f78) v2.5.1 (eef7710cb1) against this change merges
      GUI_App.cpp cleanly, since upstream did not change it. The only
      conflict, src/OrcaSlicer.cpp, is the same without this change.

[ $B = fixed ] && export APP=app-fixed || export APP=app

./launch.sh $D >/dev/null; sleep 10; ./signin_fresh.sh; ./openproj.sh
./q.sh agent 'document.querySelector("[aria-label=\"New chat\"]").click(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,2000)); const t=document.querySelector("textarea"); __setv(t,"Suggest settings for strength"); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,300)); document.querySelector("button.composer-send").click(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,2000)); return "sent: "+document.body.innerText.slice(-120).replace(/\n/g," / ")' | cut -c1-300
T0=$(date +%s); n0=$(grep -c "DELETE" standin/standin.log)
./menu.sh JusPrin "Settings…" >/dev/null; sleep 3
DEL='__byText("button","Account").click(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,800)); __byText("button","Delete account…").click(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,800)); Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("[role=dialog] button")).find(b=>b.textContent.trim()==="Delete account").click(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,2500));'
./q.sh preferences "$DEL await __snap('$N-during-reply'); return (document.querySelector('[role=dialog]')?.innerText||'no dialog: '+document.body.innerText.slice(150,400)).replace(/\n/g,' / ')" | cut -c1-400
echo "DELETE requests during reply: $(( $(grep -c DELETE standin/standin.log) - n0 ))  (t=$(( $(date +%s)-T0 ))s)"
./ev.sh $N-during-reply >/dev/null
./q.sh preferences '__byText("[role=dialog] button","Cancel")?.click(); return "ok"' >/dev/null
while [ $(( $(date +%s)-T0 )) -lt 42 ]; do sleep 2; done
./q.sh agent 'return "chat now: "+document.body.innerText.slice(-160).replace(/\n/g," / ")' | cut -c1-300
n1=$(grep -c DELETE standin/standin.log)
./q.sh preferences "$DEL await __snap('$N-after-reply'); return (document.querySelector('[role=dialog]')?.innerText||'no dialog: '+document.body.innerText.slice(150,500)).replace(/\n/g,' / ')" | cut -c1-400
echo "DELETE requests after reply: $(( $(grep -c DELETE standin/standin.log) - n1 ))"; grep DELETE standin/standin.log | tail -1
./ev.sh $N-after-reply >/dev/null
echo "account in conf: $(grep -c refusal-repro $D/JusPrin2.conf)"

./launch.sh $D JUSPRIN_AGENT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:9/v1 >/dev/null; sleep 10; ./openproj.sh
echo "== chat A after sign-out"; ./q.sh agent "return 'picker before typing: '+$PICK" | cut -c1-200; SEND "And the top layers?" $N-chatA-signed-out
echo "== brand-new chat after sign-out"; NEWCHAT $N-new-after-signout
echo "== chat B on OpenAI"; SEND "How strong will this part be?" $N-chatB-ran
./menu.sh JusPrin "Settings…" >/dev/null; sleep 3
./q.sh preferences '__byText("button","BYOAI").click(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,1000)); const rows=Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("button")).filter(b=>b.textContent.trim()==="Remove"); const r=rows.find(b=>{let n=b; for(let i=0;i<6&&n;i++){ if(/OpenAI/.test(n.innerText||"")&&!/Anthropic/.test(n.innerText||"")) return true; n=n.parentElement;} return false;}); if(!r) return "NO OPENAI REMOVE: "+rows.length; r.click(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,1500)); const c=Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("[role=dialog] button")).find(b=>/Remove/.test(b.textContent)); if(c){c.click(); await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r,1500));} return "removed"' | cut -c1-200
python3 -c "import json; a=json.load(open('$D/JusPrin2.conf'))['jusprin_agent']; print('keys now:', sorted(k for k in a if k.endswith('_api_key')), 'provider:', a.get('provider'))"
P=$(pgrep -f "$S/app(-fixed)?/JusPrin.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer"|head -1); osascript -e "tell application \"System Events\" to tell (first process whose unix id is $P) to click button 1 of window \"Preferences\"" >/dev/null 2>&1; sleep 1
echo "== chat B after its key is removed"; ./q.sh agent "return 'picker before typing: '+$PICK" | cut -c1-200; SEND "And how long will it take?" $N-chatB-key-removed
echo "== brand-new chat after key removal"; NEWCHAT $N-new-after-key-removed
